holidays.name: International Polar Bear Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the world's largest land carnivore and raise awareness about the Arctic habitat it depends on. Fans share bear photos, donate to conservation groups, and sometimes take icy plunges in solidarity.
holidays.origin: Founded by the conservation group Polar Bears International, which chose late February because it is when mother bears and newborn cubs are snug in their dens, preparing to emerge.
holidays.funFact: A polar bear's fur is not actually white. Each hair is a transparent, hollow tube that scatters light, and the skin underneath is black.

holidays.name: No Brainer Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to doing the obvious things in life that require zero overthinking. Take the nap, eat the cake, say yes to the free stuff.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance popularized through online holiday calendars as a lighthearted nudge to stop second-guessing easy decisions.
holidays.funFact: Studies on decision fatigue suggest the average adult makes thousands of decisions a day, so a day off from deliberating is arguably a scientific necessity.

holidays.name: Pokémon Day
holidays.description: A global celebration of the pocket monster franchise, with fans hosting game marathons, trading card tournaments, and special announcements from the creators, often including Pokémon Presents showcases.
holidays.origin: Pokémon Red and Green launched in Japan on February 27, 1996, for the Game Boy. The Pokémon Company now marks the anniversary each year.
holidays.funFact: The original games were developed by creator Satoshi Tajiri, who was inspired by his childhood hobby of collecting insects.

holidays.name: Open That Bottle Night
holidays.description: A night for wine lovers to finally uncork that special bottle they have been saving for the perfect occasion, and to share it with friends and good food.
holidays.origin: Created by Wall Street Journal wine columnists Dorothy Gaiter and John Brecher in 2000 after readers confessed to hoarding bottles for ages. It is held on the last Saturday of February, and some calendars list it near this date.
holidays.funFact: The columnists invented it because so many people admitted that they were afraid to open their fancy wine, and the 'perfect occasion' never seemed to arrive.

holidays.name: Chocolate Soufflé Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the airy, delicate dessert that terrifies home cooks. Bakers attempt to whip up a chocolate soufflé and pray it does not collapse.
holidays.origin: A food-lover's observance listed on culinary calendars, honoring the classic French dessert whose name comes from the word meaning 'to puff up'.
holidays.funFact: Soufflés date to early 18th-century France, and a legend says that chefs once banned slamming kitchen doors to keep the puffy desserts from deflating.
